description: Checks a project's dependencies and a person's apps. Every package with an exact version (as a lockfile pins it) is checked against every known flaw (OSV.dev, CISA's exploited list), and the incidents this site explains come first; a range, no version, or an app is only compared with those incidents. Says the answer on the site's scale (yes, mostly, kind-of, no; unknown when no exact version was sent), which packages to update and to which version. Give packages, product ids, or the text of a lockfile (package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, requirements.txt, composer.lock; with filename, any of 30+ formats: Cargo.lock, go.mod, uv.lock, Gemfile.lock...). For a public GitHub repo, check_repo reads every lockfile itself. Only names and versions reach the flaw database; nothing about who asked is stored.

filename.description: The lockfile's file name (Cargo.lock, go.mod, uv.lock...): reads it with the repo check's own readers, which also tell dev dependencies apart.

full.description: Also every flaw of every package, minor ones included. Without it: the answer, what to update and why.

lockfile.description: The whole text of a lockfile or manifest.

ecosystem.description: One of npm, PyPI, Packagist, Maven, Go, crates.io, RubyGems, NuGet, Docker, GitHub Actions, ConanCenter, Hackage, Pub, SwiftURL, Hex, CRAN, Julia (lowercase works, pip and composer too).

products.description: Product ids people install: chrome, firefox, safari, edge, windows, macos, ios, android, linux, office, whatsapp, zoom, plex, wordpress, php, nodejs, python, openssl, nginx, apache-httpd, ivanti-connect-secure, pan-os, fortimail, fortios, cisco-asa, sonicwall-sonicos, gitlab, tidb-cloud.
